decision: The later confirmation window supports approximately neutral Q8 decode timing with substantially fewer allocations; the previous5-6% slowdown was not reproduced in that limited window. No speedup or universal no-regression claim. Keep the preserved candidate available for adoption review, but do not change production in this measurement-only round. Earlier unstable data remain part of the record.

identities.provenance: Existing executables reused without rebuilding; hashes checked against the prior receipt. Historical runtime identities come from build records and the retained patch, not today's working tree. Current production remains the baseline runtime.

environment.pmset_observation: No thermal warning level, performance warning level or CPU power status had been recorded. This is not evidence of stable frequency, power, thermal conditions or core residency.
environment.limits: No CPU-core pinning or hardware counters; other host activity and memory bandwidth were not controlled. No other owned model, build, race or heavy validation jobs ran during timing. Small metadata/parser commands did run. No system-wide settings or other processes were modified.

protocol.workload: Existing BenchmarkPostSingleExpGeneration, deterministic synthetic model, prefix33/tokens128; workers1 and4, formatsf32/q8/q4. Harness asserts planned workers and sets GOMAXPROCS inside each leaf. No fresh real-model measurement, prefill sweep or short-decode sweep in this round.
protocol.stage1: Default-policy same-binary baseline/baseline screen: three fresh-process label pairs, two Q8 worker leaves per process,1s leaves; label order alternates before-after, after-before, before-after.
protocol.stage2: Diagnostic same-binary screen with taskpolicy -b applied only to child benchmark processes, otherwise stage1 settings. Background scheduling is a separate experimental condition, not core affinity or an equivalent production condition; these results are not pooled with default-policy results. Policies end with each process.
protocol.stage3: Default-policy fixed-work candidate comparison: one leaf per fresh process,32 timed generations per leaf (-test.benchtime=32x), count1; three pairs per format/worker case. Within a case, before-after order on odd blocks and after-before on even blocks. Format order rotates [f32,q8,q4], [q8,q4,f32], [q4,f32,q8]; worker order is [1,4], [4,1], [1,4]. Baseline and candidate for each case run adjacently.
protocol.stage4: Default-policy fixed-work same-binary control: one Q8 worker leaf per fresh process,32x, three pairs per worker count, same alternating label and worker orders as stage3.
protocol.stage5: After stage4 showed lower variation, an explicitly adaptive confirmation repeats stage3 unchanged. Earlier samples were not deleted, filtered or pooled away; this window was selected based on observed controls, not preregistered as an independent validation set.
protocol.stage6: Immediately after confirmation, repeat stage4 as a post-control.
protocol.inference: Ratios compare independently timed ns/op estimates, even with matched fixed iteration counts; they are not matched request timings. Three blocks per condition, no confidence interval or statistical equivalence test. Bracketing controls provide context, not a correction to subtract from candidate ratios.

screens.interpretation: Initial default screen remains unstable; background policy did not provide sufficiently stable controls. The cause of variation is not established. Near-one medians alone would conceal these swings.

first_fixed_work_pass.interpretation: Still variable: individual ratios include1.619 for FP32 workers1 and0.679 for Q8 workers4. Do not treat these medians as an adoption result.

confirmation.interpretation: Q8 is approximately baseline-like in this later, less-variable default-policy window, without the previous5-6% penalty. The small favorable ratios are not proof of acceleration: FP32 workers1 also moves by about0.8%, and Q4 workers4 by about2.6%. FP32/Q4 arithmetic is unchanged but their shared descriptor footprint differs, so they are not strictly unchanged-runtime controls. Only the baseline/baseline runs are strict same-code controls. No guarantee for earlier unstable periods, other workloads, real models or other machines.

allocation_confirmation.scope: Whole synthetic generation, including executor setup, rather than a warm-kernel allocation count. Low fixed iteration counts and scheduling can alter amortized worker-related counts. Prior warm-kernel zero-allocation evidence remains in the prior receipt; no new warm-kernel test or model output check was performed here.
allocation_confirmation.retained_tradeoff: Candidate executor struct160 bytes versus baseline120 on this architecture. This fixed-size increase is unchanged by remeasurement and is not RSS.

audit.raw_samples: All108 new benchmark stdout files retained. Each summary contains all samples, recomputed binary hashes, declared historical source identities and raw-file SHA-256. Previous records and raw files remain unchanged. Summary generation uses scripts/summarize_q4_invocation.py; for per-case prefixes, --cases 1 --runs 3 --benchtime 32x, baseline and candidate binary/source arguments as above; strict controls use the baseline identity for both labels. Initial screens use --cases 2 --benchtime 1s.
audit.production: No production source or test implementation changed. Current runtime remains ea77195bd7cb3b35a6a466bf92920db3c16dc5dc7d3ee18d5ffd0a359a7d9d08. Prior correctness/race/compatibility/model-output checks are referenced, not claimed as newly rerun. No rebuild, patch application, commit, push or PR.
